reviewer_trace: Selected the first 12 native return_* test conversations by ascending SHA-256 of 99:convo_id before reviewing customer text or individual predictions.

Reviewed every original customer turn in the selected conversations; did not view agent turns, scenario values, latent subflow labels, or individual extractor predictions when assigning supplemental intent/reason/condition labels.
Retained the separate automatic official-placeholder-grounded order-ID labels; evidence snippets remain exact original customer text.
Assigned product names only when customers explicitly named them. Generic item/it/return-label requests do not identify a product.

Mapped explicit wrong-size complaints to does_not_fit, stains to defective, explicitly received wrong-color variants to wrong_item, unspecified color dissatisfaction to other, and the explicit no-longer-needed motivation to changed_mind.

Null used/opened/damaged labels mean no explicit customer assertion of that state after reviewing all customer turns, not proof of unused/unopened/undamaged. Original packaging retention/disposal and rhetorical questions do not establish these states.
Case 8580 remains intent unclear because its customer never explicitly requests a return/refund/send-back; the latent return subflow was not used as intent evidence.
The twelve supplemental rows require independent human confirmation and are not official ABCD ReturnFacts annotations. No production extractor or prompt was changed after reviewing this subset.

intent.text: I would like to return an item

annotations.review_note: Customer retains original packaging; this says nothing explicit about opening, use, or damage. No named item or request for human transfer.

intent.text: I want to return an item

reason.text: it came in the wrong color

annotations.review_note: Wrong delivered color is reviewed as an incorrect product variant (wrong_item); this taxonomy choice needs human confirmation. No explicit condition or product-name assertion.

reason.text: they have a damn stain on them

annotations.review_note: A stain supports a defective-quality reason but not an explicit physical-damage assertion. The rhetorical mailman-use question is not a fact; discarding packaging does not explicitly state opening. Flirting is not a human-support request.

intent.text: I want to return some jeans I just bought

annotations.review_note: Color dissatisfaction is explicit, but the customer does not say the delivered color differed from the ordered one or that their mind changed. Reviewed as other; taxonomy choice needs confirmation.

intent.text: I want to return my jacket

reason.text: there is a HUGE stain on it

annotations.review_note: Stain supports defective quality; no explicit use, opening, physical-damage, or human-transfer assertion. A bare yes answer cannot establish a condition without the excluded agent question.

reason.text: it had a stain on the front right sleeve

annotations.review_note: Customer says received stained item and requests a label, without explicitly requesting a return/refund/send-back. Generic item/sleeve does not name a product. Bare yes answers are not standalone condition evidence.

intent.text: I need to return an item

annotations.review_note: Preserves the customer surface pants rather than inferring a brand/product string from catalog metadata. Diet discussion does not state use, opening, or damage. Leading zero in order ID is preserved.

intent.text: I need to make a return

annotations.review_note: Wrong delivered color is reviewed as an incorrect variant, not an unstated change of mind. No product name or explicit condition assertion.
